result.summary: Makes the `.onion` suffix check case-insensitive when parsing network addresses. This aligns Tor hostname handling with existing I2P hostname parsing and prevents uppercase `.ONION` addresses from falling back to standard DNS resolution.
result.problem: Addresses ending in uppercase `.ONION` are not recognized as Tor addresses. Instead of being parsed as Tor onion services, they fall through to regular DNS resolution, potentially causing unintended DNS queries or connection failures.
evidence: PR description: 'With the current code, a name like <addr>.ONION will not be parsed as a Tor address, and will instead fall through to regular hostname resolution.'
result.scope_notes: Small patch (+10/-2 across 2 files) modifying netaddress parsing and likely adding a unit test.
result.card: Makes the suffix check case-insensitive when parsing .onion network addresses, matching existing behavior for I2P hostnames. Currently, hostnames ending in uppercase variations like .ONION fail Tor address detection and fall through to regular DNS resolution. This fixes the privacy and connectivity issue for users configuring or receiving mixed-case Tor addresses.

risk.why: A parsing flaw could misidentify valid hostnames or fail to parse legitimate Tor addresses during peer connection setup.
